relevant_lessons: - [2026-06-27] (landing, design) A lander engine enclosed by its own interstage shroud had its exhaust blocked: full throttle, fuel draining, g-force 0 (an LV-N at trans-Mun injection). Engines that stay attached must have bare bells.

- [2026-09-30] (landing, design, eva) A 3-legged single-stack Mun lander (FL-T400 + Terrier, pod on top, LT-2 legs) rocked +-7 deg on a 5.7 deg slope and fell over twice: once when the kerbal dropped out of the hatch, once after the vessel switch that follows boarding. Use 4 legs or a wider base, and lift off promptly after boarding.

- [2026-06-27] (landing, design, eva) A tall, narrow single-stack lander tipped over on Duna, burying the hatch and blocking both the flag and the ascent. Design for a tip-over angle well above the expected slopes (wide stance, low centre of mass) and check tilt before any surface ignition.

- [2026-06-27] (landing) Mun terminal-descent failures: a fixed 30 m suicide-burn margin forced near-full throttle near the ground (bounce, drift, dry tanks); a capped hover from 250 m oscillated and burned the return fuel; lateral cleanup starting at 120 m with 7.5 m/s sideways was too late (impact at 18.8 m/s); switching to vertical while drifting preserved the slide. Null the horizontal speed before contact and stay retrograde until it is small.

- [2026-06-27] (landing) The airless hoverslam that worked on the Mun: coast until surface speed reaches v_ref(h) = √(2(f·a_max − g)h) with ~8% thrust reserve (f ≈ 0.92), then track the curve surface-retrograde; below ~70 m the curve is too steep to track, so a separate terminal controller is needed. Best touchdown: −0.1 m/s vertical, 0.2 m/s horizontal.

- [2026-06-27] (transfer) Every correction must keep the parking or return periapsis safe: one Mun correction lowered the Kerbin periapsis to 27 km and the craft reentered. For crews, prefer trajectories with a recoverable free return.

- [2026-06-27] (mun, transfer, capture) Stopping an injection burn as soon as any Mun SOI appeared gave a grazing 2.1 Mm periapsis whose capture was unaffordable; stop on a capture-grade predicted periapsis.

- [2026-06-27] (mun, transfer, landing) Finite-burn execution erased ~19 km of planned Mun periapsis (33.7 km planned, 14.4 km actual); planned periapses under ~45 km were unsafe for that craft, and "periapsis > 0" is not landing-safe because terrain rises many kilometres. The first Mun relay impacted after warping straight into a −40 km predicted periapsis: read the prediction and correct before warping in.
